section.content: 一种调节器用半导体集成电路，在切换了输出电压时，输出电压的噪音电平也不大幅变化，具备：根据输出电压所对应的反馈电压和预定的基准电压之间的电位差来控制控制用晶体管使输出电压恒定的控制电路；生成基准电压的基准电压电路；提供基准电压电路的动作电流的电流源电路；以及动作电流变动抑制电路，其进行抑制使基准电压电路的动作电流在输入电压发生变动时也不增减，在该调节器用半导体集成电路中，将上述基准电压电路即带隙基准电压电路构成为可变型基准电压电路，通过改变在基准电压的输出节点和接地点之间连接的串联电阻的一方电阻值而能够变更增益。在基准电压电路和控制电路之间设置还用于去除基准电压中包括的噪音的低通滤波器。

A semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator, which does not change a noise level of an output voltage significantly even when the output voltage is switched, comprises: a control circuit for controlling the control transistor to make the output voltage constant according to a potential difference between a feedback voltage corresponding to the output voltage and a predetermined reference voltage; a reference voltage circuit for generating a reference voltage; a current source circuit for supplying an operating current of the reference voltage circuit; and an operating current fluctuation suppression circuit for suppressing the operating current of the reference voltage circuit from increasing or decreasing even when the input voltage fluctuates, wherein the bandgap reference voltage circuit, which is the reference voltage circuit, is configured as a variable reference voltage circuit, and the gain can be changed by changing one resistance value of a series resistor connected between an output node of the reference voltage and a ground point. A low-pass filter for removing noise included in the reference voltage is provided between the reference voltage circuit and the control circuit.

Semiconductor integrated circuit for regulatorTechnical Field

The present invention relates to a reference voltage circuit of a dc power supply device, and more particularly, to a technique effective for a semiconductor integrated circuit for controlling a series regulator including a reference voltage circuit including a bipolar transistor.

Background

One of the dc power supply devices includes a series regulator that controls a control transistor to decrease an output voltage according to the output voltage and outputs a predetermined voltage. In a system in which the series regulator is used as a power supply, particularly, a series regulator used for a system in which noise is feared (for example, a high-sensitivity image sensor), it is considered to be advantageous to use a bipolar transistor as a transistor constituting a circuit.

In general, a control semiconductor integrated circuit constituting a series regulator is provided with an error amplifier, detects a potential difference between a feedback voltage corresponding to an output voltage and a predetermined reference voltage, and controls a control transistor based on the potential difference.

In a conventional semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator, as shown in fig. 8, a reference voltage circuit for generating a reference voltage (fixed) to be supplied to an error amplifier is provided inside a chip.

In recent years, a design technique of a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator is known, in which, in order to cope with various systems, for example, by switching resistance values of voltage dividing resistors (R6 or R7 in fig. 8) for generating a feedback voltage, output voltages of multiple steps such as 1.5V and 2.0V, 2.5V, and … … can be easily generated.

However, when a method (product classification) of generating a plurality of output voltages by incorporating the reference voltage circuit 12 and switching the resistance values of the voltage dividing circuits (R6, R7) for feedback as shown in fig. 8 is adopted, the error amplifier 11, the output voltage control transistor Q0, and the voltage dividing circuits (R6, R7) function as a gain-switching amplifier circuit. In this embodiment, the gain G changes as shown by the following formula G ═ Vout/Vref ═ 1+ (R7/R6) by switching the resistance value of the resistor R6 or R7. Therefore, there is a problem that the noise level included in the output of the reference voltage circuit 12 varies depending on the gain, that is, the level of the output voltage.

Further, an invention related to a constant voltage circuit (series regulator) in which a low-pass filter is provided between a reference voltage circuit and an error amplifier in order to reduce voltage noise output from the reference voltage circuit has been proposed (see patent document 1). However, the technique of patent document 1 does not disclose the idea of switching the output voltage and the above-mentioned problems accompanying the idea of configuring a circuit with a MOS transistor that is inferior to a bipolar transistor in terms of noise reduction.

On the other hand, patent document 2 discloses that a bandgap circuit is used as a reference voltage circuit in a series regulator control semiconductor integrated circuit including a bipolar transistor. However, the technique of patent document 2 realizes a power supply circuit (corresponding to the bias circuit of the present invention) that generates an operating voltage of a reference voltage circuit in order to improve ripple suppression characteristics. Patent document 2 also does not disclose the idea of switching the output voltage and the above-described problems associated with the idea.

Patent document 1: japanese patent application laid-open (JP-A): 2011 an 22689

Patent document 2: japanese patent application laid-open (JP-A): 2001-84043 publication

Disclosure of Invention

The present invention was made in view of the above circumstances, and an object thereof is to provide a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator in which a noise level of an output voltage does not change greatly even when the output voltage is switched.

Another object of the present invention is to provide a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator capable of suppressing a variation in output voltage even if a variation occurs in input voltage.

In order to achieve the above object, a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator according to the present invention includes:

a control transistor connected between an input terminal to which a direct-current voltage is applied and an output terminal;

a control circuit that controls the control transistor so that an output voltage is constant, based on a potential difference between a feedback voltage based on the output voltage and a predetermined reference voltage;

a reference voltage circuit that generates the reference voltage;

a current source circuit for supplying an operating current of the reference voltage circuit; and

an operating current fluctuation suppression circuit for suppressing the operating current of the reference voltage circuit from increasing or decreasing even when the voltage input to the input terminal fluctuates,

the operating current fluctuation suppression circuit includes: a first transistor connected in series between a power supply line for supplying an operating current to the reference voltage circuit and a ground line connected to a ground potential point, a base terminal of the first transistor being connected to a node for outputting the reference voltage,

the reference voltage circuit is configured to include:

a second transistor, a first resistor, and a second resistor connected in series between the power supply line and a ground line;

a third transistor, a fourth transistor, a third resistor, and a fourth resistor connected in series between the power supply line and a ground line;

a fifth transistor and a sixth transistor connected in series between the power supply line and a connection node of the third resistor and the fourth resistor,

the fifth transistor has a base terminal and a collector terminal connected to each other and functions as a current-voltage conversion element, and has a base terminal connected to the base terminal of the third transistor,

a base terminal of the second transistor is connected to a connection node between the third transistor and the fourth transistor,

base terminals of the fourth transistor and the sixth transistor are connected to a connection node between the first resistor and the second resistor or a connection node between the second transistor and the first resistor, and a potential of the connection node between the second transistor and the first resistor or a potential of the connection node between the first resistor and the second resistor is taken out as the reference voltage,

the gain is determined according to the resistance value of the first resistor.

According to the above-described means, a regulator in which the noise level of the output voltage does not change significantly can be realized even when the output voltage is switched. Further, since the variable reference voltage circuit is configured as a circuit that integrates a circuit that generates the reference voltage and a circuit that amplifies the reference voltage, the number of elements constituting the circuit can be reduced, the dedicated area of the circuit can be reduced, and the chip size can be reduced. Further, since the operating current fluctuation suppression circuit for suppressing the operating current of the reference voltage circuit is provided, the reference voltage generated by the reference voltage circuit can be stabilized even if the input voltage fluctuates, and a ripple suppression effect can be obtained in which the output voltage does not vary according to the input.

Further, since the operating current fluctuation suppression circuit is constituted by the first transistor connected between the power supply line for supplying the operating current to the reference voltage circuit and the ground line connected to the ground potential point and the base terminal of the transistor is connected to the node for outputting the reference voltage, the operating current flowing through the reference voltage circuit is suppressed from fluctuating even if the input voltage fluctuates, and the circuit can be realized by a simple circuit with a small number of elements.

Further, it is preferable that a low-pass filter for removing noise included in the reference voltage is provided between the reference voltage circuit and the control circuit.

Thus, noise included in the reference voltage generated by the reference voltage circuit can be removed by the low-pass filter, and thus the degree of change in the noise level of the output voltage when the output voltage is switched can be reduced as compared with the conventional method in which the gain of the control circuit is changed. That is, it is possible to reduce the difference in noise level between products (series regulators) classified according to the potential of the output voltage.

Further, it is preferable to provide a voltage dividing circuit including resistors connected in series, the voltage dividing circuit dividing the output voltage to generate a feedback voltage to be supplied to a control circuit (error amplifier), the gain being changed by adjusting a resistance value of the first resistor constituting the reference voltage circuit, thereby changing a level of the output voltage in steps, and the trimming for finely adjusting fluctuation of the output voltage due to manufacturing variation being performed by adjusting a resistance value of the resistor constituting the voltage dividing circuit for generating the feedback voltage.

Thus, in a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator which includes a variable reference voltage circuit and can change the level of an output voltage in stages, it is possible to easily achieve the accuracy of the output voltage when fine-tuning the fluctuation of the output voltage.

According to the present invention, it is possible to realize a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator in which the noise level of the voltage output from the reference voltage circuit does not change significantly even when the output voltage is switched. Further, a semiconductor integrated circuit for a regulator can be realized which can suppress the fluctuation of the output voltage even if the input voltage fluctuates. Further, there is an effect that the reference voltage circuit in which the reference voltage is variable can be realized with a small number of elements.

Description of reference numerals

10: regulator IC, 11: error amplifier (control circuit), 12: reference voltage circuit, 13: bias circuit (current source circuit), 14: low-pass filter, 15: clamp circuit (operating current suppression circuit), 16: amplifier circuit, Q0: and an output voltage control transistor.

Detailed Description

Preferred embodiments of the present invention will be described below with reference to the accompanying drawings.

Fig. 1 shows an embodiment of a series regulator (including LDO) to which the present invention is applied. Although not particularly limited, in fig. 1, elements constituting a circuit of a portion surrounded by a dashed line are formed on 1 semiconductor chip and constitute a control semiconductor integrated circuit (hereinafter referred to as a regulator IC)10 of the regulator.

The regulator IC10 of this embodiment is configured such that an output voltage control transistor Q0 formed of a PNP bipolar transistor is connected between a voltage input terminal IN to which a dc voltage Vin from a dc voltage source is applied and an output terminal OUT, and voltage dividing resistors R6 and R7 for dividing the output voltage Vout are connected IN series between the output terminal OUT and a ground terminal GND to which a ground potential is applied. The voltage VFB divided by the voltage dividing resistors R6 and R7 is fed back to the non-inverting input terminal of the error amplifier 11 which controls the gate terminal of the output voltage control transistor Q0.

The error amplifier 11 controls the output voltage control transistor Q0 based on the potential difference between the feedback voltage VFB and the reference voltage Vref, and controls the output voltage Vout to a desired potential. The series regulator of this embodiment operates by maintaining the output voltage Vout at a predetermined voltage by the feedback control described above. The potential of the output voltage Vout is set by the magnitude of the reference voltage Vref from the reference voltage circuit 12 and the resistance ratio of the voltage dividing resistors R6 and R7. The output terminal OUT is connected to an OUT-band output capacitor for stabilizing the output voltage Vout.

The regulator IC10 of the present embodiment is provided with a terminal Pc to which a signal for ON/OFF control of the regulator is externally input (ON/OFF), a bandgap reference voltage circuit 12 for generating a reference voltage Vref, a bias circuit 13 for generating an operating current of the reference voltage circuit 12, and a low-pass filter 14 provided between the reference voltage circuit 12 and the error amplifier 11 for suppressing noise included in the output of the reference voltage circuit 12.

The bias circuit 13 controls its operation by an ON/OFF control signal ON/OFF externally input to the terminal Pc. The low-pass filter 14 is composed of a resistor Rn integrated with a chip (on-chip) formed on a semiconductor substrate, and an external capacitor Cn connected to an external terminal provided on the chip.

Next, the reference voltage circuit 12 and the bias circuit 13 of the embodiment of fig. 1 are explained.

The reference voltage circuit 12 of this embodiment is connected to a power supply line LL at a collector terminal of a PNP transistor Q7 whose emitter terminal is connected to a voltage input terminal IN and whose base current is controlled by a bias circuit 13, and supplies an operating current via a Q7 and the power supply line LL.

The reference voltage circuit 12 includes: a PNP transistor Q2 and resistors R1, R2 connected in series between the power supply line LL and a ground line connected to the ground terminal GND; a PNP transistor Q3, an NPN transistor Q4, and resistors R3, R4 connected in series between the power supply line LL and the ground line (GND); and a PNP transistor Q5 and an NPN transistor Q6 connected in series between the power supply line LL and the connection node N3 of the resistors R3 and R4.

Among these elements, the transistor Q5 functions as a current-voltage conversion element by connecting the base terminal and the collector terminal, and the current mirror circuit is configured by commonly connecting the base of Q3 and the base of Q5. The base terminal of the transistor Q2 is connected to the collector terminal of the transistor Q3, and a current flows through the resistors R1 and R2. Base terminals of the transistors Q6 and Q4 are commonly connected to a connection node N2 of the resistors R1 and R2. The transistors Q6, Q4 are designed to be 1: 8(Q6< Q4) is given a bias.

In the reference voltage circuit 12 of this embodiment, the base current of the Q2 is controlled by the bias voltage of the transistors Q6, Q4 and the resistor R3, so that the base potential of the transistors Q6, Q4, that is, the potential of the node N2 becomes the voltage Vz based on the band gap of the semiconductor (silicon) of the substrate material. The emitter current of Q2 is also controlled by controlling the base current of Q2, and an arbitrary voltage Vref amplified by the resistance ratio is generated at a node N1 by the bandgap voltage Vz, which is the potential of the node N2, and the resistors R1 and R2. Specifically, a voltage obtained by multiplying the bandgap voltage Vz by (R1+ R2)/R2, that is, a voltage represented by Vref Vz × (R1+ R2)/R2 is generated at the node N1 and output as the reference voltage Vref.

The regulator IC10 of the present embodiment is designed and manufactured as an IC that performs classification such that, for example, by changing a film (mask) for forming wiring, the resistance value of R1 of the resistors R1 and R2 constituting the reference voltage circuit 12 is switched to output, as the output voltage Vout, any one of voltages of a plurality of steps, for example, 1.5V, 2.0V, and 2.5V … …. That is, the resistor R1 is regarded as a kind of variable resistor. Further, by making the resistor R1 a variable resistor, the reference voltage Vref generated at the contact N1 can be changed, and the reference voltage circuit 12 functions as a variable reference voltage source.

Further, the resistance value of R2 is switched to determine the level of the output voltage Vout, and the voltage dividing resistor R6 and R7 for generating the feedback voltage VFB are trimmed (fine-tuned) to ensure the accuracy of the output voltage Vout. As a method of adjusting the output voltage Vout to a desired value, a method of trimming the resistance value of the resistor R1 is also considered, but since the resistance value of the resistor R1 directly affects the gain of the reference voltage circuit 12, there is an advantage that the accuracy of the output voltage Vout can be easily achieved in the resistance value of the trimming resistor R6 (or R7) as compared with the resistance value of the trimming resistor R1.

The bias circuit 13 includes: a PNP transistor Q8 and resistors R8, R9 and an NPN transistor Q10 connected IN series between the voltage input terminal IN and the ground line; a resistor R10 and an NPN transistor Q9 connected IN series between the voltage input terminal IN and a connection node of the resistor R9 and the transistor Q10; and resistors R11, R12 connected in series between the control terminal Pc to which the ON/OFF control signal ON/OFF is input and the ground.

The base terminal of the transistor Q10 is connected to a connection node N5 between the resistors R11 and R12, and the base terminal of the transistor Q9 is connected to a connection node N4 between the resistors R8 and R9.

Further, the base terminal of the transistor Q7 is connected to the collector terminal of the transistor Q8, the bias circuit 13 performs ON/OFF control by an ON/OFF control signal ON/OFF, a bias voltage of a predetermined potential is generated at the collector terminal of the transistor Q8 in the ON state, a base current of the transistor Q7 flows by the bias voltage, and an operating current flows to the reference voltage circuit 12 from the transistor Q7.

Specifically, if the ON/OFF control signal is set to a potential of 5V by a system control device such as a microprocessor, a collector current flows through the transistor Q10, the bias circuit 13 is activated, and a current flows through the transistor Q7 for current supply. Therefore, the bias circuit 13 and the transistor Q7 function as a current source circuit that generates an operating current of the reference voltage circuit 12.

Further, the regulator IC10 of the present embodiment is provided with a clamp circuit 15 including an NPN transistor Q1 connected between the power supply line LL and the Ground (GND), and the clamp circuit 15 has a function of controlling so that the operating current of the reference voltage circuit 12 does not vary even if the dc voltage Vin applied to the input terminal IN varies. For example, if the input voltage Vin becomes high, the operating current flowing from the transistor Q7 to the reference voltage circuit 12 side increases, but if the current flowing through the clamp circuit 15 at this time increases, the change in the operating current of the reference voltage circuit 12 is suppressed, whereas if the input voltage Vin becomes low, the operating current flowing from the transistor Q7 to the reference voltage circuit 12 side decreases, but at this time the current flowing through the clamp circuit 15 decreases, and the change in the operating current of the reference voltage circuit 12 is suppressed. That is, the clamp circuit 15 has a function of clamping a current, which does not change the operating current of the reference voltage circuit 12 even if the input voltage Vin changes.

Next, the operations of the reference voltage circuit 12 and the clamp circuit 15 will be described in more detail.

If the input voltage Vin becomes higher and the current of the transistor Q7 increases, the potential of the power supply line LL becomes higher and the collector current of the transistor Q2 increases, and the potentials of the nodes N1 and N2 rise. Accordingly, collector currents of the transistors Q6, Q4 increase. However, since R4 is connected between the emitters of the transistors Q4 and Q6, the collector current of the transistor Q4 is limited by the bias voltages of the transistors Q4 and Q6 and the resistor R3, and the collector current does not increase as much as that of the transistor Q6. In addition, if the collector current of Q6 is to be increased, then current is drawn from diode-connected transistor Q5, the current of Q5 increases, and Q5 also increases as does Q3, which constitutes a current mirror. However, the collector current of Q4 is limited by resistor R3, so the current drawn from the base of Q2 is reduced. If the base current of Q2 decreases, the collector current of Q2 also decreases, and as a result, the potential rise at nodes N1 and N2 is suppressed, and the fluctuation of the reference voltage Vref is suppressed.

Further, if the input voltage Vin becomes high, the current of the transistor Q7 increases, and the potential of the power supply line LL also becomes high, but the voltage between the emitter and the base of Q1 becomes large because the node N1 suppresses the variation of the reference voltage Vref by the operation of the reference voltage circuit, but the collector current of the transistor Vbe-Ic characteristic Q1 increases, and the voltage of the power supply line LL decreases. The power supply line LL is stabilized by the voltage at the node N1 + the emitter-base voltage Vf of the Q1.

When the input voltage Vin becomes lower and the current of the transistor Q7 decreases, the potential of the nodes N1 and N2 of the reference voltage circuit 12 decreases by the operation opposite to the above operation, but the base current of Q2 increases and the collector current of Q2 increases, thereby suppressing the decrease in the potential of the nodes N1 and N2. In addition, if the input voltage Vin drops, the transistor Q1 constituting the clamp circuit 15 decreases the emitter-base voltage of the transistor Q1, but the collector current according to the Vbe-IC characteristic Q1 of the transistor decreases, and the voltage of the power supply line LL increases, thereby suppressing the variation in the power supply voltage of the reference voltage circuit 12.

As described above, the clamp circuit 15 has a function of clamping a current so that the operating current of the reference voltage circuit 12 does not change even if the input voltage Vin changes. In addition, since the potential of the power supply line LL, which is a power supply voltage applied to the reference voltage circuit 12, is stabilized by the current flowing through the clamp circuit 15 changing in accordance with the variation of the input voltage Vin, in other words, the clamp circuit 15 has a function of clamping the voltage so that the power supply voltage of the reference voltage circuit 12 does not change even if the input voltage Vin changes.

Further, by performing the above operation, the clamp circuit 15 suppresses the ripple of the output voltage Vout without changing the reference voltage Vref generated by the reference voltage circuit 12 even if the input voltage Vin changes. That is, the clamp circuit (transistor Q1) brings about an effect of suppressing the ripple of the output voltage.

Fig. 2 shows the results of simulation investigation of PSRR (power supply voltage variation removal ratio) characteristics of the output voltage Vout, with respect to the case where the clamp circuit 15 is provided in the regulator IC10 of the present embodiment and the case where the clamp circuit 15 is not provided. In fig. 2, the horizontal axis represents the frequency of the ripple component of the input voltage Vin, the solid line a represents the PSRR characteristic when the clamp circuit 15 is provided, and the broken line B represents the PSRR characteristic when the clamp circuit 15 is not provided. As is clear from fig. 2, the ripple suppression effect of the reference voltage circuit 12 is greatly improved by providing the clamp circuit 15, and the characteristic is excellent, particularly in the range of DC to 1kHz, which is close to 20dB when the clamp circuit 15 is provided.

The regulator IC10 of the present embodiment is provided with a low-pass filter 14 between the reference voltage circuit 12 and the error amplifier 11, resistors R1 and R2 for gain adjustment are provided in the output section of the bandgap reference voltage circuit 12, and the potential of the output voltage Vout is switched by switching the resistance value of R1. Therefore, as shown by a solid line a in fig. 3, compared with the regulator IC of the related art in which the potential of the output voltage Vout is switched by switching the resistance value of R6 of the resistors R6 and R7 constituting the voltage dividing circuit for generating the feedback voltage VFB, the amount of change in the noise level included in the output voltage depending on the product class can be reduced. A broken line B in fig. 3 indicates how the noise level included in the output voltage generated when the output voltage is switched in the conventional regulator IC shown in fig. 8 changes according to the product class (horizontal axis).

Further, as a circuit for switching the potential of the output voltage Vout, for example, as shown in fig. 4, a variable gain type amplifier circuit 16 having a differential amplifier AMP and voltage dividing resistors R13 and R14 may be provided at a stage subsequent to the fixed type reference voltage circuit 12, but the circuit of fig. 4 has a larger dedicated area than the regulator IC of the present embodiment shown in fig. 1.

Specifically, if the circuit of fig. 4 is represented at an element level, the circuit shown in fig. 5 is obtained. In fig. 5, reference numeral 12 is a reference voltage circuit, reference numeral 13 is a bias circuit, and reference numeral 16 is a variable gain type amplification circuit. According to fig. 5, the variable reference voltage circuit 12 of fig. 1 requires 10 elements in total of 4 PNP transistors, 2 NPN transistors, and 4 resistors, and the fixed reference voltage circuit 12 of fig. 4 requires 3 PNP transistors, 2 NPN transistors, and 3 resistors, and further requires 21 elements in total of 3 PNP transistors, 2 NPN transistors, and 3 resistors as elements constituting the amplification circuit 16. That is, the regulator IC shown in fig. 4 requires 11 elements more than the regulator IC of the present embodiment. Therefore, the regulator IC of the present embodiment (fig. 1) has an advantage that the number of elements can be reduced, the area dedicated to the circuit can be reduced, and the chip size can be reduced, as compared with the regulator IC of fig. 4.

Fig. 6 and 7 show modifications of the series regulator IC of the embodiment of fig. 1.

These modifications are modifications when the present invention is applied to a regulator IC for constituting a negative power supply.

The difference between the negative power supply regulator IC of fig. 6 and the positive power supply regulator IC of fig. 1 is that, IN the modification of fig. 6, a negative power supply voltage VEE is input to the input terminal IN, an NPN bipolar transistor having different conductivity types is used as the transistor Q7 for supplying an operating current to the output voltage control transistor Q0 and the reference voltage circuit 12, and a level shift circuit (level shift circuit)17 is provided for converting ON/OFF control signals of GND (0V) to Vcc levels input to the control terminal Pc into ON/OFF control signals of VEE to GND (0V) levels. The bias circuit 13 may be of the same construction as the circuit shown in fig. 1.

The reference voltage circuit 12 and the clamp circuit 15 in the regulator IC of this modification operate similarly to the circuit of fig. 1, and have the following advantages as in the circuit of fig. 1: even if the output voltage is switched, the amount of change in the noise level included in the output voltage can be reduced, and the dedicated area of the circuit can be reduced. Further, since the clamp circuit 15 is provided, the ripple suppression effect of the output voltage can be obtained.

In the modification of fig. 7, instead of generating the reference voltage Vref obtained by amplifying the bandgap-based voltage Vz by the resistors R1 and R2, the reference voltage Vref obtained by dividing the bandgap-based voltage Vz by the resistors R1 and R2 is generated. The other structure is the same as the modification of fig. 6. In the case of this modification, in addition to the effect of the modification of fig. 6, there is an advantage that the noise included in the bandgap voltage Vz can be compressed and the effect of further reducing the noise can be obtained because the reference voltage Vref is generated by dividing the voltage Vz by the resistors R1 and R2.

The present invention has been described specifically by the present inventors based on the embodiments, but the present invention is not limited to the embodiments. For example, the characteristic configuration as in the modification of fig. 7 can be adopted for the adjuster IC of the embodiment of fig. 1.

In the above embodiment, the clamp circuit 15 that suppresses increase and decrease of the operating current of the reference voltage circuit 12 in accordance with the fluctuation of the input voltage is provided in parallel with the reference voltage circuit 12, but a circuit having the same function may be provided in series with the reference voltage circuit 12.

Further, in the above-described embodiment, the outer band element is used as the capacitor Cn constituting the low-pass filter 14, but the capacitor Cn may be formed as an element integrated on a chip.
